added_models.model: CD33 rs12459419 splice-site genotype (human genetic predictor of CD33 V-domain antibody benefit)

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The predictor's own data are gemtuzumab's (not a member): set aside, not scored (decision 13); the track opens untested until a member is tested.
efficacy.note: Lamba built the predictor on gemtuzumab (AAML0531): CC genotype relapse 26% vs 49% with GO, no GO benefit in CT/TT; untested on any member.
efficacy.quote: Our results suggest that patients with the CC genotype for rs12459419 have a substantial response to GO, making this a potential biomarker for the selection of patients with a likelihood of significant response to GO.
efficacy.judgement: Opened as its own patient-level track: the brief admits people with a loss-of-function genotype (the T allele skips exon 2, removing the IgV epitope that SGN-CD33A and gemtuzumab share) and a model built on a sibling drug (product_in_model false). Dated to Lamba's epub (2017-06-23); registry_date is AAML0531 (NCT00372593, first posted 2006-09-07). Rule question 6 is pending with the adjudicator.

efficacy.model_src: Lamba 2017, doi:10.1200/JCO.2016.71.2513 (CD33 rs12459419 genotype vs gemtuzumab benefit, COG AAML0531)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: CR/CRi rate by genotype: predicted CC > CT/TT, observed 30% vs 30%
efficacy.confidence_note: n = 20 (10 per genotype group), retrospective genotyping of phase 1 patients; the source calls itself limited by sample size. Gale 2018's adult gemtuzumab null is a non-member datum, set aside. EFS and OS nulls are in the same letter; no separate outcome trial.
efficacy.note: 20 SGN-CD33A patients (mono or +HMA): CR/CRi 3/10 CC vs 3/10 CT/TT, EFS and OS not associated; the predicted genotype-restricted benefit did not appear.
efficacy.short: Genotype did not predict SGN-CD33A response
efficacy.quote: This genotype, for the CD33 splice site SNP rs12459419, was not associated with clinical response (30% CR/CRi in both groups), event-free survival, or overall survival.

patient_trials.quote: There was no significant difference in response between patients carrying the most common genotype, CC (n = 10), and those carrying CT or TT genotypes (n = 10)

efficacy.reason: No genotype effect on member response rate
efficacy.judgement: contra, not retro: the predictor (2017) predates its test on a member, and Stanchina genotyped already-treated phase 1 patients to test it, so retrodiction is false. comparison_stated true: the letter states the shared-epitope expectation itself and sets it beside SGN-CD33A outcomes. magnitude 'null': the predicted difference was absent, not reversed. poc_gate follows the draft's handling of the phase 1 CR/CRi rate (NCT01902329 primary was AEs). Patient-level: one member's miss colours the track.

added_models.model: Cord-blood CD33-CAR-NK (4-1BB, sIL-15) in NSG Molm13-luc xenografts + HSC colony assay

engagement.confidence_note: Proxy date: the registry record (first posted 2021-08-17) of the trial run on this model; the preclinical experiments are undated in Huang 2025.
engagement.note: Model readouts were Molm13 lysis, IL-15 secretion and xenograft bioluminescence; no PD readout was carried into the trial design.
engagement.short: Model readouts: lysis, IL-15, xenograft BLI
engagement.quote: Targeting CD33 surface antigens by CAR NK cells provides an off-the-shelf immune cell therapy.
engagement.judgement: Opener at a proxy date: the trial that started 2021-12-23 was designed on this model's xenograft and HSC-toxicity results (Huang 2025), so the model existed by 2021; the registry record stands in for the undated preclinical work.

engagement.confidence_note: Full text read. The xenograft measured tumour bioluminescence only.
engagement.note: Patients' CAR-NK qPCR peaked 6 h post-infusion and faded; the model measured no persistence or PD readout, so nothing was compared.
engagement.short: Patient qPCR persistence has no model counterpart
engagement.quote: CD33 CAR-NK cells could be observed by qPCR within 7 days. The peak concentration occurred 6 h after each infusion, followed by a second peak within two days of the initial peak.
engagement.judgement: untested, not same: engagement scores the readout the model used (adjudication of engagement 2); the xenograft measured tumour bioluminescence, which is efficacy, and no occupancy, persistence or NK-activation readout exists on the model side.

dose.confidence_note: Proxy date: the registry record (first posted 2021-08-17) of the trial run on this model; the preclinical experiments are undated in Huang 2025.
dose.note: Mice received 1 x 10^7 CAR-NK cells; the model stated no cell-dose target for patients.
dose.quote: Targeting CD33 surface antigens by CAR NK cells provides an off-the-shelf immune cell therapy.
dose.judgement: Opener at a proxy date: the trial that started 2021-12-23 was designed on this model's xenograft and HSC-toxicity results (Huang 2025), so the model existed by 2021; the registry record stands in for the undated preclinical work.

dose.confidence_note: Full text read; the quote is a verbatim fragment of the dose-rationale sentence.
dose.note: Doses (6 x 10^8 to 1.8 x 10^9 cells, no DLT) came from prior CAR-T/CAR-NK trials, not the model; silence is untested.
dose.short: Doses set from clinical precedent, not model
dose.quote: Considering the existing CAR-T-cell and CAR-NK-cell trials, we designed a two-stage exploratory trial
dose.judgement: Follows the adjudication of dose 4 on the antibody track: the model stated no exposure, cell-dose or regimen target, so a tolerated dose reached in patients is patient-side only and nothing was compared.

efficacy.confidence_note: Proxy date: the registry record (first posted 2021-08-17) of the trial run on this model; the preclinical experiments are undated in Huang 2025.
efficacy.note: Molm13-luc xenografts were cleared 12 days after CAR-NK infusion, matching CD33 CAR-T; the trial opened on that result.
efficacy.quote: Targeting CD33 surface antigens by CAR NK cells provides an off-the-shelf immune cell therapy.
efficacy.judgement: Opener at a proxy date: the trial that started 2021-12-23 was designed on this model's xenograft and HSC-toxicity results (Huang 2025), so the model existed by 2021; the registry record stands in for the undated preclinical work.

efficacy.model_src: Huang 2025 (same paper), doi:10.1186/s40164-024-00592-6: NSG Molm13-luc xenografts cleared 12 days after CAR-NK infusion
efficacy.magnitude_basis: response rate; xenograft clearance not quantified against a remission rate
efficacy.confidence_note: Single-centre, single-arm, n = 10; one durable remission (bridged to HSCT), median PFS 71.5 days. The trial may have been public as an EHA 2023 abstract (HemaSphere P522, PMC10429699, no DOI indexed): if rule question 5 admits supplement abstracts the entry re-dates to 2023.
efficacy.note: Phase 1 (n=10, median 5 prior lines): 6/10 MRD-negative CR at day 28, a co-primary; the xenograft's clearance held, but remissions were short.
efficacy.quote: By day 28, six of ten patients had achieved minimal residual disease (MRD)-negative complete remission.

patient_trials.quote: The median progression-free survival (PFS) was 71.5 days (range, 44–258 days), and the overall survival (OS) was 137 days (range, 50–258 days) for patients with complete remission

efficacy.judgement: same on the registered co-primary (ORR at 4 weeks), so endpoint_role primary. comparison_stated true because one paper reports model and trial and draws the joint conclusion ('Our preclinical and clinical data demonstrated the primary efficacy and safety'); it does not quantify the match, so magnitude is direction_only. Short durability does not change the primary-endpoint call and is noted.

safety.confidence_note: Proxy date: the registry record (first posted 2021-08-17) of the trial run on this model; the preclinical experiments are undated in Huang 2025.
safety.note: The model predicted limited HSC toxicity (colony assay, mouse) relative to CAR-T; an animal cannot show CRS or ICANS.
safety.quote: Targeting CD33 surface antigens by CAR NK cells provides an off-the-shelf immune cell therapy.
safety.judgement: Opener at a proxy date: the trial that started 2021-12-23 was designed on this model's xenograft and HSC-toxicity results (Huang 2025), so the model existed by 2021; the registry record stands in for the undated preclinical work.

safety.model_src: Huang 2025 (same paper), doi:10.1186/s40164-024-00592-6: CD33 CAR-NK showed limited toxicity to HSCs in the colony assay and no HSC damage in mice
safety.magnitude_basis: reversibility of marrow suppression; the model's colony counts were not set against patient cytopenia grades
safety.confidence_note: n = 10; Flu/Cy lymphodepletion confounds early cytopenias; the stated prediction (HSC sparing relative to CAR-T) is judged on recovery without allo-HSCT rescue. One grade 2 CRS is not a miss: a mouse cannot show CRS.
safety.note: Grade 3-4 cytopenias in most patients after Flu/Cy resolved in a median 27 days without HSCT rescue; one grade 2 CRS, no ICANS/GVHD.
safety.quote: Additionally, all instances of severe bone marrow suppression resolved within one month, highlighting the favorable safety profile of the treatment.
safety.judgement: same, not partial: the model's stated prediction was sparing of HSCs relative to CD33 CAR-T's prolonged aplasia, and every severe cytopenia recovered within a month without transplant rescue; the paper itself calls the profile favourable. Grade 4 neutropenia in 4/10 is recorded in the note.
